question.text: In the SEBI AML framework, what should happen when a client has been accepted but is subsequently found to be a Politically Exposed Person (PEP)?

answer.text: The account must be immediately closed
The intermediary should continue business without any additional measures
The intermediary shall obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship
The matter should be reported to the police

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI AML framework provides that where a client has been accepted and the client or beneficial owner is subsequently found to be, or subsequently becomes, a PEP, the registered intermediary shall obtain senior management approval to continue the business relationship. The Trap: Option A seems like a safe approach, but being a PEP is not itself illegal. It triggers enhanced due diligence and senior management oversight rather than automatic account closure. Note: Intermediaries should also verify the source of funds and source of wealth of PEPs as part of the additional measures applicable to such clients.
